content.topic: Public transport use in a city
content.prompt:
The graph below shows the average number of passengers per day using four types of public transport in a European city between 1988 and 2018.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
content.figure_title: Average daily passengers by type of public transport, 1988–2018
key_features: Overview: the underground grew the most and became by far the most used type of transport, while bus use rose and then declined; the tram fell and then recovered strongly, and suburban rail changed very little.
The underground more than doubled, from 80,000 to 185,000 passengers a day, and overtook the bus between 2003 and 2008.
Bus use peaked at 135,000 in 1998 and then fell steadily to 92,000 by 2018, below its 1988 level.
The tram dropped to a low of 30,000 in 1998 and then almost tripled to 88,000, overtaking suburban rail by 2013 and nearly matching the bus by 2018.
Suburban rail was the most stable series, rising only slightly from 60,000 to 69,000 over the 30 years.
